targetReport.description: Madagascar's resources law for its three-tier Collectivités Territoriales Décentralisées (Communes, Régions, Provinces), verified via direct download (hosted on the electoral commission CENI's own site, mirroring the full official text). KEY FINDING — Art. 194, the Impôt Synthétique repartition formula: "La répartition du produit de l'impôt synthétique... se fait comme suit : - 50% au profit du budget de la Commune ; - 30% au profit du budget de la Région ; - 10% au profit du budget de la Province ; - 10% au profit du Fonds national de péréquation." Further shared-tax formulas: Art. 195 (hydrocarbon royalty): 40% Commune / 30% Région / 10% Province / 20% Fonds national de péréquation; Art. 206 (telecom-mast tax): 50% Communes / 30% Régions / 20% Provinces. Art. 198-204 list commune-exclusive local taxes (civil-protection/dangerous-animal tax, a 'taxe de résidence pour le développement' explicitly earmarked for Fokontany-level development financing, a water/electricity-subscriber tax).

targetReport.title: Lei n.° 1/2008, de 16 de Janeiro — Regime financeiro, orçamental e patrimonial das autarquias locais e o Sistema Tributário Autárquico
targetReport.description: Mozambique's municipal finance law, verified via a Wayback Machine capture (2011) of the originating Ministério da Administração Estatal PDF, which is now offline (mae.gov.mz unreachable) — same primary text, accessed via the earliest available archival mirror rather than a dead live host. KEY FINDING — Art. 43(2): "O montante do Fundo de Compensação Autárquica é objecto de uma dotação própria a inscrever no Orçamento do Estado e é constituído por 1,5% das receitas fiscais previstas no respectivo ano económico" [The Fundo de Compensação Autárquica (FCA) amount is set by its own appropriation in the State Budget and consists of 1.5% of the fiscal revenue projected for the relevant economic year]. Art. 43(3): the fund's proceeds are "de afectação livre pelas autarquias beneficiárias" [freely allocable by the recipient municipalities]. Art. 44's distribution formula: "FCAa = NHa/NHT x 75%FCA + Ata/ATT x 25%FCA" — each municipality's share is 75% weighted by its population share (Número de Habitantes) and 25% by its territorial-area share (Área Territorial). Art. 51 lists the municipal tax system: Imposto Pessoal Autárquico, Imposto Predial Autárquico (IPRA), Imposto Autárquico de Veículos, Imposto Autárquico de Sisa, Contribuição de Melhorias, plus fee-based (not tax-based) 'taxas por Licenças Concedidas e por Actividade Económica.'
targetReport.cadence_note: One-off foundational legal instrument (still in force as of this round; not superseded by Lei 12/2023, which governs institutional structure rather than finance).

results.basis: Oil Sands Royalty Regulation, 2009 (AR 223/2008) s.29 sets the gross royalty rate as RG% = 1% + [FG (A - B)], where FG is '8% divided by $65 per barrel', A is 'the lesser of the WTI price for the given month ... and $120 per barrel' and B is 'the lesser of A for the month and $55 per barrel'. s.29(3)(a) defines the monthly WTI price as 'the simple average of the WTI prices for the trading days of the preceding month, excluding any days where the trading price was at or below $0 per barrel', and s.29(4)(a) defines the daily WTI price as 'the settlement price for the day of the prompt month contract of West Texas Intermediate crude futures as traded on NYMEX'. The same A term drives the post-payout net royalty percentage factor, NRPF = 25% + (FN (A - B)).
results.evidenceQuote: the settlement price for the day of the prompt month contract of West Texas Intermediate crude futures as traded on NYMEX

targetReport.title: Valuation of Land Act 1960 (Vic)
targetReport.description: The Victorian analog to NSW's Valuation of Land Act 1916: establishes the office of Valuer-General (Part I) and requires an annual general valuation of rateable land statewide. Section 11 (as substituted by No. 69/2011 s.53): a valuation authority must 'cause a general valuation of rateable land within an area to be made as at 1 January in each calendar year' and, 'before 30 April that year,' cause it to be returned and provided to the relevant council. VERIFIED DIRECTLY: the official source (legislation.vic.gov.au) is a JS-rendered SPA whose raw HTML doesn't yield section text via regex, and the AustLII mirror is Cloudflare-blocked in this environment; full consolidated text instead fetched and confirmed via a third-party legal mirror, the FAO Legal Office's legislation database (faolex.fao.org), then extracted with pdftotext.
targetReport.cadence_note: Section 11 mandates a genuinely annual valuation cycle (valuation date 1 January, return due before 30 April each calendar year) -- unlike NSW, where the Valuation of Land Act 1916 requires annual ascertainment in principle but current council practice runs on an operational three-year cycle. Victoria's own valuations-process page confirms the Valuer-General has been the single valuation authority for all 79 Victorian councils since 2023.

release_schedule.note: The Valuation of Land Act 1960 (Vic) is a piece of Victorian legislation, not a recurring statistical/administrative publication. Victoria's official legislation register (legislation.vic.gov.au) shows a version-history/reprint page with 70+ consolidated versions dating back to 1997, with new versions issued whenever amending Acts or statutory rules take effect (e.g. 4 Dec 2024, 1 Jan 2025, 1 Jul 2025 - three updates within about seven months). There is no fixed cadence, calendar, or stated rule governing when the next amendment/reprint will occur; it is amended irregularly by the Victorian Parliament as needed. This is a foundational legal instrument, not a true recurring release.

targetReport.title: Property Assessment Notice and Assessment Roll (Current Value Assessment)
targetReport.description: Ontario's single province-wide property assessment, prepared by a not-for-profit corporation funded by all Ontario municipalities rather than by a government department. This is the structural difference from Alberta, where each municipality prepares its own roll and the province must then run an explicit equalization step to make them comparable. Ontario needs no equalization because there is one assessor. The standard is Current Value, defined in the Assessment Act s. 1(1) as 'the amount of money the fee simple, if unencumbered, would realize if sold at arm's length by a willing seller to a willing buyer'. MPAC states it uses 'one of three approaches to value properties: direct comparison approach, income approach, cost approach', with the direct comparison approach 'the most commonly used' and the choice depending on 'property type, and the number of recent comparable sales of similar properties in the area'. The returned roll and its household counts are what the Ontario Municipal Partnership Fund allocates against.
targetReport.cadence_note: The roll returns annually; the values in it have not been re-based since 2016, and the gap between those two facts is the point. The Assessment Act s. 19.2(1) sets a four-year cycle by schedule, and para 4 assigns 1 January 2016 to 'the four taxation years from 2017 to 2020'. MPAC states the schedule has been suspended: 'On August 16, 2023, the Ontario government filed a regulation to amend the Assessment Act, extending the postponement of a province-wide reassessment through the end of the 2021-2024 assessment cycle. Property assessments for the 2026 property tax year will continue to be based on fully phased-in January 1, 2016 current values.' So `releases_per_year` 1 counts the returned roll, which does move for new construction, demolition and change of use; `changes_per_year` 0.25 is the statutory reassessment cycle, which is the rate at which the valuation basis is supposed to move and has not moved in ten years. Both numbers are true and neither alone describes this node.

release_schedule.note: MPAC delivers an assessment roll annually to Ontario municipalities each Nov-Dec (with Property Assessment Notices mailed to owners with changed assessments in November, and the roll formally 'returned' in early-mid December: Dec 12 2023, Dec 10 2024, ~Dec 9 2025). This annual notice/roll cycle is distinct from the province-wide Current Value Assessment (CVA) base-year update: Ontario's Assessment Act nominally requires reassessment on a 4-year cycle, but the government has repeatedly postponed it by regulation since 2020 (most recently confirmed through the 2026 tax year), so assessed values remain frozen at January 1, 2016 current values with no announced date for the next province-wide reassessment. The annual roll-return/notice cycle, however, has continued on schedule every year regardless of the reassessment freeze.

targetReport.title: Property Assessment Notice and Assessment Roll (Current Value Assessment)
targetReport.description: Ontario's single province-wide property assessment, prepared by a not-for-profit corporation funded by all Ontario municipalities rather than by a government department. This is the structural difference from Alberta, where each municipality prepares its own roll and the province must then run an explicit equalization step to make them comparable. Ontario needs no equalization because there is one assessor. The standard is Current Value, defined in the Assessment Act s. 1(1) as 'the amount of money the fee simple, if unencumbered, would realize if sold at arm's length by a willing seller to a willing buyer'. MPAC states it uses 'one of three approaches to value properties: direct comparison approach, income approach, cost approach', with the direct comparison approach 'the most commonly used' and the choice depending on 'property type, and the number of recent comparable sales of similar properties in the area'. The returned roll and its household counts are what the Ontario Municipal Partnership Fund allocates against.
targetReport.cadence_note: The roll returns annually; the values in it have not been re-based since 2016, and the gap between those two facts is the point. The Assessment Act s. 19.2(1) sets a four-year cycle by schedule, and para 4 assigns 1 January 2016 to 'the four taxation years from 2017 to 2020'. MPAC states the schedule has been suspended: 'On August 16, 2023, the Ontario government filed a regulation to amend the Assessment Act, extending the postponement of a province-wide reassessment through the end of the 2021-2024 assessment cycle. Property assessments for the 2026 property tax year will continue to be based on fully phased-in January 1, 2016 current values.' So `releases_per_year` 1 counts the returned roll, which does move for new construction, demolition and change of use; `changes_per_year` 0.25 is the statutory reassessment cycle, which is the rate at which the valuation basis is supposed to move and has not moved in ten years. Both numbers are true and neither alone describes this node.

release_schedule.note: No formal Executive decree fixing the exact 2030 date/collection period has been located; IBGE's own president has publicly referred to work on a "Censo 2030" (discussing hybrid/technological collection methods), and a Brazilian news outlet (Estado de Minas, Jan 2026) states "a próxima grande contagem da população brasileira está prevista para 2030". This restores the original decennial cycle (2000, 2010, 2020→2022 delayed, 2030) rather than counting 10 years forward from the delayed 2022 edition (which would suggest 2032). Exact month/day of collection is not yet published.

targetReport.title: SADC Harmonised Consumer Price Index (HCPI) Newsletter
targetReport.description: A regional harmonised CPI compiled from national CPIs. The September 2012 issue (Stage I) names all its covered states verbatim: "Botswana, Democratic Republic of Congo, Lesotho, Madagascar, Malawi, Mauritius, Mozambique, Namibia, Seychelles, South Africa, Swaziland, United Republic of Tanzania, Zambia and Zimbabwe" — all eight of this corpus's Southern Africa countries (ZA, BW, NA, LS, SZ, ZM, MW, ZW) are named individually, by country. Methodology, verbatim: "the HCPI development must generally be in compliance with the international standards relating to development of Consumer Price Indices (CPI)," constructed as "weighted averages of the national HCPIs, using as weights each country's total household consumption expenditure converted to a common currency using the 2005 purchasing power parities." Excludes Education and Health divisions at this Stage I development level.
targetReport.cadence_note: Titled a monthly newsletter, but the SADC document-listing page shows an irregular actual publication history (entries from 2012 through a September 2022 issue, not evenly spaced) — recorded honestly rather than assuming the titled cadence holds in practice.

release_schedule.note: Grande Spirit Foundation (a regional Alberta 'management body' under the Alberta Housing Act) requisitions operating funds annually from its member municipalities (City/County of Grande Prairie and several surrounding towns/counties/MDs). The Housing Act provision found only specifies that a municipality must pay its agreed contribution within 90 days of the Foundation mailing the invoice -- it does not fix a date by which the Foundation must issue the requisition. Board meeting minutes show requisition percentage increases being approved at a mid-year (June 2024) meeting for the following fiscal year's budget, but no calendar, fixed statutory date, or consistent multi-year pattern for the requisition's own issuance could be confirmed -- the Foundation's public board-minutes archive (2023-2025) contains no dedicated 'requisition schedule' document, and the Alberta Housing Act / Housing Regulation full text could not be retrieved (qp.alberta.ca, kings-printer.alberta.ca, canlii.org, and open.alberta.ca all blocked or errored on fetch). Member-municipality budget documents (e.g. County of Grande Prairie) show the requisition amount folded into municipal interim/final budgets each Nov-Dec, but that reflects the municipality's own budget cycle, not a documented Foundation release date.

results.basis: RESOLVED 2026-08-09 (browser/websearch session, closing G.64.md cheap check 2). The Bank of Canada's own explainer states the mechanism: 'What's behind your mortgage rate' (bankofcanada.ca, May 27, 2020) -- 'These include the prime rate, which is used by the banks as a basis for pricing variable-rate mortgages.' Typed uses_data_from rather than calculated_from, matching this file's own boc-prime-rate -> boc-policy-rate precedent: the explainer describes a market convention (prime plus or minus a lender-set spread), not a formula stated by the published series' own methodology page, and the published aggregate is a volume-weighted average of what banks actually charged rather than a recalculation of prime itself.
results.evidenceQuote: These include the prime rate, which is used by the banks as a basis for pricing variable-rate mortgages.

targetReport.title: Chartered Bank Prime Lending Rate
targetReport.description: The rate Canadian chartered banks quote as the basis for variable-rate lending — mortgages, lines of credit, most consumer and small business borrowing. Set by each bank rather than by the central bank, and published by the Bank of Canada as part of Canadian interest rates. In practice the single number through which monetary policy reaches a household budget.
targetReport.cadence_note: Published weekly, but changes only when banks move it, which is normally within a day of a policy rate change. Cadence of publication and cadence of change are different things — a distinction the pulse simulation currently cannot express.

entries.covers: Weekly Chartered Bank Prime Lending Rate update

release_schedule.rule: Typically published on Wednesdays by 14:30 ET.
release_schedule.note: The Bank of Canada's Prime Rate series (posted interest rates offered by chartered banks) is updated weekly, with the page stating it is 'Typically published on Wednesdays by 14:30 ET.' The table's most recent entries prior to the 2026-08-11 reference date were 2026-07-08, 07-15, 07-22, 07-29, and 08-05 (all Wednesdays), consistent with the stated weekly cadence and with the corpus's existing releases_per_year=52. Next occurrence computed as the following Wednesday after 2026-08-11.

results.window: Changes in the policy interest rate lead to similar changes in short-term interest rates. A policy-rate change can also affect long-term interest rates, especially if people expect that change to be long-lasting.

4. National accounts statistics 
 National accounts statistics, representing the nationwide economic status, is compiled according to System of National Accounts (SNA) 2008, published jointly by United Nations, World Bank, International Monetary Fund, Organization of Economic Cooperation and Development, Commission of the European Communities. The advance estimates are released by one month after the end of the reference quarter, preliminary results are compiled in the successive month and published in the second half of February, May, August and November, after reviewing by the Committee of National Accounts.

targetReport.title: European System of Accounts 2010 (ESA 2010)
targetReport.publisher: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
targetReport.description: The EU's national accounts framework, enacted as Regulation (EU) No 549/2013. Article 1(2) sets out its two parts: 'a methodology (Annex A) on common standards, definitions, classifications and accounting rules that shall be used for compiling accounts and tables on comparable bases for the purposes of the Union' and 'a programme (Annex B) setting out the time limits by which Member States shall transmit to the Commission (Eurostat) the accounts and tables'. Unlike the international standards already in this corpus, ESA 2010 is a Regulation — member states do not adopt it by choice — which is why the EU branch was expected to produce supranational-to-national edges the Canada/US pair lacks. Annex B turned out to name tables and deadlines rather than publications; see the _dropped entries here and in eu-draft-budget.json.
targetReport.cadence_note: A generational standard, revised roughly once every fifteen to twenty years: ESA 1995 preceded it, and a further revision is already anticipated. releases_per_year matches sna-2008 (0.05) so the two read at the same pulse rate; see _open_questions.

release_schedule.rule: The Labour Cost Survey (Arbeitskostenerhebung) is conducted every four years under EU law (Council Regulation (EC) No 530/1999 and Commission Regulation (EC) No 1737/2005) and Germany's Verdienststatistikgesetz, covering reference years 2000, 2004, 2008, ..., 2020, 2024, 2028. Eurostat's LCS metadata states 'Data for LCS2024 will be published in 2nd half of 2026,' and Destatis's April 2026 press release (PD26_148_624) states the 2024 survey results 'werden voraussichtlich im Juli 2026 veröffentlicht' (are expected to be published in July 2026).
release_schedule.note: As of the research date (2026-08-11), no press release or dataset confirming the actual July 2026 publication of AKE2024 detailed results could be located via search — the target month has just passed and the release may have slipped slightly (Destatis used 'voraussichtlich' = 'expected'). The prior cycle (LCS2020) was published July 2022 (PD22_280_624), i.e. about 2 years after the reference year, consistent with the 2024→2026 pattern. If AKE2024 has already been published by the time this is read, the next occurrence would instead be AKE2028, expected to be published in the second half of 2030.

results.basis: Council Regulation (EC) No 479/2009, consolidated text of 01/09/2014, Article 1(1): 'For the purposes of the Protocol on the excessive deficit procedure and of this Regulation, the terms in paragraphs 2 to 6 are defined according to Regulation (EU) No 549/2013 of the European Parliament and the Council of 21 May 2013 on the European system of national and regional accounts in the European Union (hereinafter referred to as ESA 2010). The codes in brackets refer to ESA 2010.' The dependence is operative, not decorative: Article 1(2) defines 'Government' as 'the sector of general government (S.13)... as defined in ESA 2010', Article 1(3) defines 'Government deficit (surplus)' as 'the net borrowing (net lending) (B.9) of the sector of general government (S.13), as defined in ESA 2010', and Article 1(5) defines 'Government debt' by ESA 2010 categories 'currency and deposits (AF.2); debt securities (AF.3) and loans (AF.4)'. 'Are defined according to' is derivation language and is not on Research.1.md section 5a's watchlist. Direction: the EDP Regulation is the dependent, ESA 2010 the depended-on. Re-fetched and re-read from EUR-Lex 2026-08-07 after G.50.md Finding 4 recorded the site serving nothing; the outage was transient. Quoted with EUR-Lex's in-line amendment markers stripped — the unstripped Article 1(1) reads with the whole clause inside a M2 insertion marker, because the original 2009 text referred to ESA 95.

It matters here for Article 9, which compels into existence a published national document class that no other instrument this branch has followed produces: 'Member States shall provide the Commission (Eurostat) with a detailed inventory of the methods, procedures and sources used to compile actual deficit and debt data and the underlying government accounts' (Art. 9(1)), 'The inventories shall be updated following revisions in the methods, procedures and sources adopted by Member States' (Art. 9(3)), and 'Member States shall make their inventories public' (Art. 9(4)). Eurostat's own EDP inventories page states the consequence — 'Pursuant to Article 9 of Council regulation 479/2009 (as amended), all EU Member States are required to prepare and publish an EDP inventory' — and carries a live Inventory link for each of the 27. EUR-Lex titles it a '(Codified version)', codifying Council Regulation (EEC) No 3605/93. Note that the Regulation names no member state's inventory by title: AGENCY ONLY at exactly the point where a title would have produced a downward edge.

targetReport.title: European System of Accounts 2010 (ESA 2010)
targetReport.publisher: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
targetReport.description: The EU's national accounts framework, enacted as Regulation (EU) No 549/2013. Article 1(2) sets out its two parts: 'a methodology (Annex A) on common standards, definitions, classifications and accounting rules that shall be used for compiling accounts and tables on comparable bases for the purposes of the Union' and 'a programme (Annex B) setting out the time limits by which Member States shall transmit to the Commission (Eurostat) the accounts and tables'. Unlike the international standards already in this corpus, ESA 2010 is a Regulation — member states do not adopt it by choice — which is why the EU branch was expected to produce supranational-to-national edges the Canada/US pair lacks. Annex B turned out to name tables and deadlines rather than publications; see the _dropped entries here and in eu-draft-budget.json.
targetReport.cadence_note: A generational standard, revised roughly once every fifteen to twenty years: ESA 1995 preceded it, and a further revision is already anticipated. releases_per_year matches sna-2008 (0.05) so the two read at the same pulse rate; see _open_questions.

release_schedule.note: 2030 is Eurostat's stated aim, not a locked legal date — the ESA 2030 proposal is still in consultation.

results.basis: SOR/2007-303 s. 8(1)(y), the payroll-tax revenue base, makes SEPH a named term in a statutory formula: 'P is the gross dollar value, before deductions, of the payrolls of all employers in the province for the calendar year that ends in the fiscal year, as determined by Statistics Canada on the basis of its Survey of Employment, Payrolls and Hours, other than the payrolls of (i) employers not included in that survey, and (ii) employers in the following industry classifications, as defined by the North American Industry Classification System: (A) the elementary and secondary schools industry group, (B) the hospitals subsector, (C) the nursing and residential care facilities subsector, (D) the provincial and territorial public administration subsector, and (E) the local, municipal and regional public administration subsector'. `calculated_from` because P is a term in the formula, not a consideration — the same test that makes boc-bank-rate calculated_from the policy rate. Note the provision also carves out its own exclusions by NAICS classification, so the edge to `naics` is stated in the same sentence. SCOPE, stated because the section number alone overstates it: s. 8 sits in DIVISION 2 — Nova Scotia, and defines revenue base 'For the purpose of sections 3.71 to 3.9 of the Act', which are the Nova Scotia additional-equalization provisions. SEPH does NOT appear in the DIVISION 1 all-provinces revenue base at s. 5 — the phrase 'payrolls' occurs nowhere in ss. 1 through 8(1)(j), because the 2007 reform folded payroll taxes into the personal-income base. So this is the Equalization Program depending on SEPH through one division of the Regulations, not through the general formula.

MERGED 2026-08-09 (EU/G.73.md): this one edge was defined three times across two slices — twice in equalization-named-products.json and once here — so `npm run validate`'s last-wins load dropped two of the three bases silently, taking two independent statutory citations with them. All three are preserved below; the two duplicate objects were deleted from equalization-named-products.json and this object, the only one carrying a reference_period, was kept.

(a) SOR/2007-303 s. 3.1 (DIVISION 1 definitions) names the framework three times, once for each of three capital-formation aggregates: 'gross fixed capital formation in intellectual property products, as determined by Statistics Canada on the basis of data for or from its System of Macroeconomic Accounts'; 'gross fixed capital formation in machinery and equipment, as determined by Statistics Canada on the basis of data for or from its System of Macroeconomic Accounts'; 'gross fixed capital formation in non-residential structures, as determined by Statistics Canada on the basis of data for or from its System of Macroeconomic Accounts'. Minted 2026-08-08 (Thomas, Q1, Open-Questions-2026-08-08-sweep.docx): the framework is a node in its own right, matching the statute's own wording verbatim rather than an inferred release.
[evidence: https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2007-303/page-2.html]

(b) SOR/2007-303 s. 5(b)(i), the DIVISION 1 all-provinces revenue base: 'the portion of the aggregate of corporate profits in Canada, before the payment of income taxes and without any deduction of the aggregate of corporate losses in Canada, that is attributable to any of the 10 provinces for the calendar year that ends in the fiscal year, as determined by Statistics Canada for the purpose of its System of Macroeconomic Accounts'. A fourth, independent citation of the framework, distinct from the three capital-formation terms in s. 3.1. Minted 2026-08-08, same ruling.
[evidence: https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2007-303/page-3.html]

(c) Two further terms of the same formula at SOR/2007-303 s. 8(1)(y) are pinned to the national accounts. 'A is the total wages and salaries excluding supplementary labour income, as determined by Statistics Canada for the purpose of its System of Macroeconomic Accounts, paid in the province in the calendar year that ends in the fiscal year, other than the wages and salaries paid by (i) the federal general government sector to employees in the defence industry, and (ii) the provincial and territorial general government sector and the local general government sector to their employees'. And 'M is military pay and allowances, excluding supplementary labour income, paid in the province in the calendar year that ends in the fiscal year, as determined by Statistics Canada for the purpose of its System of Macroeconomic Accounts'. RESOLVED 2026-08-08 (Thomas, Open-Questions-2026-08-08-sweep.docx Q1): the Regulations name the *System of Macroeconomic Accounts* itself, not a specific release, and Thomas's ruling was to mint the framework as its own node rather than infer a mapping to one of its releases. Target repointed from the inferred statcan-national-accounts (IMDB record 1901, GDP by income and expenditure) to statcan-system-macroeconomic-accounts, which now matches the statutory wording verbatim rather than through a judgement call. This sidesteps, rather than resolves, the still-open statcan-hfce / statcan-national-accounts duplication question recorded in statcan-macro-accounts.json — that question is about which release-level node is authoritative and remains open on its own terms.
results.evidenceQuote: gross fixed capital formation in intellectual property products, as determined by Statistics Canada on the basis of data for or from its System of Macroeconomic Accounts

targetReport.title: Canadian System of Macroeconomic Accounts
targetReport.description: The overarching accounting framework Statistics Canada operates under for macroeconomic statistics -- the umbrella that the quarterly income-and-expenditure accounts (statcan-national-accounts, IMDB record 1901), monthly GDP by industry (statcan-gdp-monthly), the Supply and Use Tables (statcan-sut) and the National Balance Sheet Accounts all sit inside, per the User Guide's own chapter structure and per record 1901's language describing the annual benchmarks as arising 'through the construction of annual supply and use tables' within this system. Minted as a node in its own right 2026-08-08 because two federal fiscal-transfer regulations (SOR/2007-303, both the Equalization and Territorial Formula Financing divisions) name the framework itself -- not a specific release -- as the thing a statutory wage/salary term is 'determined... for the purpose of': 'as determined by Statistics Canada for the purpose of its System of Macroeconomic Accounts'. Thomas's ruling (2026-08-08, Open-Questions-2026-08-08-sweep.docx Q1): frameworks and legislative instruments a regulation is built on are worth a node even with no cadence of their own -- 'its sole role is broadcasting and that needs represented.' No releases_per_year: this is an evergreen framework, not a periodic release, the same shape as the one-off foundational instruments already in the corpus.

targetReport.title: European System of Accounts 2010 (ESA 2010)
targetReport.publisher: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
targetReport.description: The EU's national accounts framework, enacted as Regulation (EU) No 549/2013. Article 1(2) sets out its two parts: 'a methodology (Annex A) on common standards, definitions, classifications and accounting rules that shall be used for compiling accounts and tables on comparable bases for the purposes of the Union' and 'a programme (Annex B) setting out the time limits by which Member States shall transmit to the Commission (Eurostat) the accounts and tables'. Unlike the international standards already in this corpus, ESA 2010 is a Regulation — member states do not adopt it by choice — which is why the EU branch was expected to produce supranational-to-national edges the Canada/US pair lacks. Annex B turned out to name tables and deadlines rather than publications; see the _dropped entries here and in eu-draft-budget.json.
targetReport.cadence_note: A generational standard, revised roughly once every fifteen to twenty years: ESA 1995 preceded it, and a further revision is already anticipated. releases_per_year matches sna-2008 (0.05) so the two read at the same pulse rate; see _open_questions.

release_schedule.note: 2030 is Eurostat's stated aim, not a locked legal date — the ESA 2030 proposal is still in consultation.

release_schedule.note: This is a methodological/compilation manual, not a periodic statistical release. targetReport.title: Council Regulation (EC) No 479/2009 on the application of the Protocol on the excessive deficit procedure
targetReport.description: The EDP Regulation — the instrument that turns the Treaty's excessive deficit procedure into a statistical reporting regime, and the second EU Regulation in this corpus to be modelled as a node after esa-2010. It matters here for Article 9, which compels into existence a published national document class that no other instrument this branch has followed produces: 'Member States shall provide the Commission (Eurostat) with a detailed inventory of the methods, procedures and sources used to compile actual deficit and debt data and the underlying government accounts' (Art. 9(1)), 'The inventories shall be updated following revisions in the methods, procedures and sources adopted by Member States' (Art. 9(3)), and 'Member States shall make their inventories public' (Art. 9(4)). Eurostat's own EDP inventories page states the consequence — 'Pursuant to Article 9 of Council regulation 479/2009 (as amended), all EU Member States are required to prepare and publish an EDP inventory' — and carries a live Inventory link for each of the 27. EUR-Lex titles it a '(Codified version)', codifying Council Regulation (EEC) No 3605/93. Note that the Regulation names no member state's inventory by title: AGENCY ONLY at exactly the point where a title would have produced a downward edge.
targetReport.cadence_note: Derived from an observed amendment record, not from a stated rate — see _open_questions. Adopted 25 May 2009; EUR-Lex lists exactly two consolidated versions, 19/08/2010 and 01/09/2014, with 01/09/2014 flagged as the current version. Two amendments across the 17 years to 2026.

release_schedule.note: April notification is provisional, October carries the revised annual figures. The underlying legal deadline (Reg. 479/2009 Art. 3(1)) is fixed at before 1 April and 1 October each year, so future cycles can be projected from that even without the exact transmission date.

results.basis: ESA 2010, Annex A, Chapter 1, paragraph 1.22 (as staged, not independently re-verified live this session -- see _open_questions): 'The ESA 2010 contains EU-specific classifications, e.g. Classification of products by activity (CPA) ... for products and NACE Rev. 2 for industries (both are harmonised with the corresponding UN classifications).' The 'harmonised with the corresponding UN classifications' clause is the §5a trap (not a dependency, not used as one); the operative clause -- ESA 2010 'contains' and uses CPA for products -- is read as the dependency, on the same footing as a survey's methodology page stating it classifies respondents by NAICS.

targetReport.title: Statistical Classification of Products by Activity in the European Economic Community (CPA)
targetReport.publisher: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
targetReport.description: Established by Regulation (EC) No 451/2008. Article 1(1): 'This Regulation establishes a new common CPA within the Community in order to ensure relevance with respect to the economic reality and comparability between national, Community and international classifications and hence national, Community and international statistics.' Article 3: 'The Commission shall use the CPA for all statistics classified according to products by activity.' A six-level hierarchical structure (Article 2(1)): sections, divisions, groups, classes, categories, subcategories. CPA Version 2.2 has applied for data transmissions since 1 January 2025. One-off foundational instrument per Research.1.md §4 (a classification standard, same shape as naics/isic/anzsic already in this corpus) -- amended periodically (2.1, 2.2) but read here from its current consolidated form, not as a recast lineage with its own cadence.

results.basis: Quality report on national and regional accounts, 2025 edition (KS-01-25-052), Executive summary, page 5: 'The quality report covers a number of quality indicators (completeness, revision policy and practice, punctuality, coherence and documentation on methodology), adhering to the requirements for the Single Integrated Metadata Structure, which were endorsed by the European Statistical System Committee in November 2015.' 'Adhering to the requirements for' is obligation language, not §5a agreement language. THIS EDGE IS THE SLICE'S HEADLINE: the Implementing Regulation that governs this report declines to name SIMS, calling it only 'the European Statistical System standards on quality reporting published by the Commission (Eurostat)' (recital 5), and a search of the whole instrument for 'SIMS', 'Single Integrated', 'ESMS', 'ESQRS' and 'Handbook' returns zero hits. The report names it. Read from the source PDF 2026-08-07.

targetReport.title: Single Integrated Metadata Structure (SIMS)
targetReport.publisher: Eurostat, endorsed by the European Statistical System Committee
targetReport.description: The ESS's single reporting structure for quality and reference metadata, formed by unifying the two earlier structures. Eurostat's own metadata-standards page: 'SIMS is the inventory and conceptual framework for all ESS quality and reference metadata concepts.' Its live status is stated in the present tense on Eurostat's quality-reporting page: 'The ESS quality reporting standard is the Single Integrated Metadata Structure (SIMS).' The two structures it absorbed remain visible as subsets rather than separate publications: 'the Euro-SDMX metadata structure (ESMS): the ESMS is a subset of SIMS' and 'the ESS standard quality report structure (ESQRS): the ESQRS is a subset of SIMS focusing on detailed quality concepts' - which is why neither is a node here.
targetReport.cadence_note: Versions, not issues. The EHQMR's lineage statement: 'the two standards - ESQRS and ESMS - were combined in the Single Integrated Metadata Structure (SIMS), which was published in 2013. Minor updates were made in 2015 and SIMS 2.0 was adopted by the European Statistical System Committee.' Eurostat's quality-reporting page additionally lists 'Single Integrated Metadata Structure Guidelines v2.0 (2019)'. Three dated points across 2013-2019; 0.2 is the observed rate, and no stated review interval was found.

release_schedule.note: SIMS is a metadata standard/conceptual framework endorsed by the European Statistical System Committee, not a periodic statistical release. It has been revised twice in its history: v1.0 (~2009) and v2.0 (November 2015, ESSC-endorsed). No Eurostat, CROS, or interoperable-europe.ec.europa.eu page states a review cycle, revision schedule, or next planned update. Commission Recommendation (EU) 2023/397 references SIMS concepts for reference metadata reporting but does not establish a periodic revision cadence. Given the absence of any calendar or stated rule, and only two revisions in ~15+ years with no announced next version, this is best classified as irregular rather than assigning a fabricated periodicity.

targetReport.title: European Statistics Code of Practice
targetReport.publisher: European Statistical System Committee (published by Eurostat)
targetReport.description: The ESS's self-regulatory quality standard, adopted by the European Statistical System Committee and applying to Eurostat and the national statistical authorities. Eurostat's own page: 'The European Statistics Code of Practice (CoP) is the cornerstone of the quality framework and sets the standards for developing, producing and disseminating European statistics. It defines 16 key principles for the institutional environment under which the EU and national statistical authorities operate, as well as for the statistical processes and output . It also includes a set of 84 indicators for the best practices and standards for each of the 16 principles.' The current edition's own title page reads 'Adopted by the European Statistical System Committee 16th November 2017'. It names its own place in a three-part framework: 'The common quality framework of the European Statistical System is composed of the European Statistics Code of Practice, the Quality Assurance Framework of the European Statistical System and the general quality management principles'.
targetReport.cadence_note: Revised editions, not periodic issues. Eurostat's 'History of the CoP' table gives three dated events and nothing else: '24 February 2005 Adoption of the CoP by the Statistical Programme Committee | September 2011 Revision of the CoP based on the results of the 1st round of ESS peer reviews | November 2017 Revision of the CoP based on the results of the 2nd round of ESS peer reviews'. Two revisions across twelve years is roughly one every six; 0.17 is that observed interval, not a stated commitment. Same treatment as the versioned-standard nodes (esa-2010, sna-2008).

release_schedule.note: No fixed periodicity found. Eurostat's director publicly flagged (Nov 2025) that a revision is 'urgently' being prepared, but no date has been set.

dissemination of European statistics. In addition to the Czech Statistical Office, eight Other National
Authorities, mainly ministries, are involved in the development, production, and dissemination of
European statistics.

inadequacies, notably as regards access to privately held data and the need for political-level approval

attempting to reopen the Statistics Act as not promising, especially given its strong provisions as

management. Reflecting the basic strengths of the Central Statistics Office and the clear directions set for the future

concern compliance with the European Statistics Code of Practice and a great many have the character
of staying the course already set. RECOMMENDATIONS
I.

targetReport.title: Single Integrated Metadata Structure (SIMS)
targetReport.publisher: Eurostat, endorsed by the European Statistical System Committee
targetReport.description: The ESS's single reporting structure for quality and reference metadata, formed by unifying the two earlier structures. Eurostat's own metadata-standards page: 'SIMS is the inventory and conceptual framework for all ESS quality and reference metadata concepts.' Its live status is stated in the present tense on Eurostat's quality-reporting page: 'The ESS quality reporting standard is the Single Integrated Metadata Structure (SIMS).' The two structures it absorbed remain visible as subsets rather than separate publications: 'the Euro-SDMX metadata structure (ESMS): the ESMS is a subset of SIMS' and 'the ESS standard quality report structure (ESQRS): the ESQRS is a subset of SIMS focusing on detailed quality concepts' - which is why neither is a node here.
targetReport.cadence_note: Versions, not issues. The EHQMR's lineage statement: 'the two standards - ESQRS and ESMS - were combined in the Single Integrated Metadata Structure (SIMS), which was published in 2013. Minor updates were made in 2015 and SIMS 2.0 was adopted by the European Statistical System Committee.' Eurostat's quality-reporting page additionally lists 'Single Integrated Metadata Structure Guidelines v2.0 (2019)'. Three dated points across 2013-2019; 0.2 is the observed rate, and no stated review interval was found.

release_schedule.note: SIMS is a metadata standard/conceptual framework endorsed by the European Statistical System Committee, not a periodic statistical release. It has been revised twice in its history: v1.0 (~2009) and v2.0 (November 2015, ESSC-endorsed). No Eurostat, CROS, or interoperable-europe.ec.europa.eu page states a review cycle, revision schedule, or next planned update. Commission Recommendation (EU) 2023/397 references SIMS concepts for reference metadata reporting but does not establish a periodic revision cadence. Given the absence of any calendar or stated rule, and only two revisions in ~15+ years with no announced next version, this is best classified as irregular rather than assigning a fabricated periodicity.

results.basis: ESS handbook for quality and metadata reports, s. 3.2.2 (p.25): 'The definitions and compilation methods for the QPIs are specified in the ESS Guidelines for the Implementation of the ESS Quality and Performance Indicators.' The Handbook takes the definitions and the compilation methods for the indicators it requires from the named document, which is methodology_depends_on rather than cites. Deliberately NOT built on the adjacent 'SIMS incorporates the 16 standard ESS Quality and Performance Indicators (QPIs)' sentence, which is a part_of statement about the indicator set and not an input claim about the document; see the caveat entry.
results.evidenceQuote: The definitions and compilation methods for the QPIs are specified in the ESS Guidelines for the Implementation of the ESS Quality and Performance Indicators.

targetReport.title: ESS Guidelines for the Implementation of the ESS Quality and Performance Indicators
targetReport.description: The document that defines the sixteen standard ESS Quality and Performance Indicators (QPIs) and states how each is computed. Its own title page reads 'ESS GUIDELINES FOR THE IMPLEMENTATION OF THE ESS QUALITY AND PERFORMANCE INDICATORS (QPI)' and 'Version 1.4'. The ESS Handbook for Quality and Metadata Reports names it as the source of the definitions: 'The definitions and compilation methods for the QPIs are specified in the ESS Guidelines for the Implementation of the ESS Quality and Performance Indicators.' NOTE, and this is the reason the node is the Guidelines document and not 'the QPIs': the indicators themselves live inside SIMS and the ESQRS as sub-concepts ('SIMS incorporates the 16 standard ESS Quality and Performance Indicators (QPIs) within the sub-concepts (for user reports) and as sub-concepts of their own (for producer reports)'), which is the same part_of shape that keeps ESMS and ESQRS out of this slice. The indicator set is part of SIMS; the document that defines it is not.
targetReport.cadence_note: Versions, not issues, and the rate is a judgement between two readings that the document does not settle. Its own p.1: 'These indicators were reviewed by the Eurostat Expert Group on Quality Indicators in 2010 and then slightly updated by the Task Force on Quality Reporting in 2012-2013' - producing Version 1.4, which Eurostat's Tools and standards list dates as 'ESS Quality and Performance Indicators (2014)'. Read narrowly, that is two revision events across 2010-2014, roughly one every two years. Read across the observed lifetime, it is two revisions and then nothing at all for the twelve years to 2026. 0.13 is the lifetime reading (2 revisions / 16 years), chosen as the conservative one and the same treatment ess-quality-assurance-framework already carries; the narrow reading is recorded here rather than discarded. No stated review interval was found in the document or on Eurostat's quality-reporting page.

release_schedule.note: This is a methodological guidance document (defining the 18 ESS Quality and Performance Indicators), not a periodic statistical release. It has been revised occasionally, reproduced within the broader 'ESS Handbook for Quality Reports' / 'ESS Handbook for Quality and Metadata Reports' series: 2009 edition, 2014 edition (the version at the corpus's current URL), a 2020 edition (Feb 2020, KS-GQ-19-006), and a 're-edition 2021' (Dec 2021, KS-GQ-21-021). Gaps between editions are irregular (5 years, then 6 years, then ~1.75 years). The 2020 handbook states revisions are proposed via periodically-convened Task Forces of the Working Group on Quality in Statistics, with no fixed/stated cycle or calendar. No edition newer than the 2021 re-edition was found as of 2026-08-11.

targetReport.title: Productive Safety Net Programme Phase 5 (PSNP5) Design Document
targetReport.publisher: Government of Ethiopia (Ministry of Agriculture) with donor partners
targetReport.description: Ethiopia's flagship rural safety-net programme, now in its fifth phase. VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session (direct fetch of the Design Document, hosted via the EU's capacity4dev platform): Text Box 5 states 'Adequacy of transfers will be addressed through annual adjustments to the wage rate in line with consumer price index (CPI) to protect its real value.' Independently corroborated from the funding side (Grok's round): a World Bank results-framework indicator for the programme reads 'Increase in average wage rate relative to the annual general CPI increase, for cash transfers beneficiaries' -- two different documents, government-authored and donor-authored, both treating the wage-CPI link as real. This is a real-terms CPI-anchoring principle, similar in shape to Egypt's statutory pension floor, though PSNP5's own instrument is a programme design document rather than primary legislation -- a different evidentiary tier worth being precise about. The docx's more specific wheat-equivalency figures (15kg/16.95kg per month) remain unconfirmed -- see _open_questions.
targetReport.cadence_note: Wage-rate review conducted annually, before June each year per the docx's own quote (not independently re-confirmed this session against the fetched content).

release_schedule.note: The PSNP5 Design Document is a one-off program design document produced by the Ethiopian Ministry of Agriculture (with donor partners including the EU and World Bank) for the fifth phase of the Productive Safety Net Programme, covering 2021-2025 (source: capacity4dev.europa.eu library entry 'Ethiopia Productive Safety Net Programme 2021-2025 Phase V Design Document, FDRE Ministry of Agriculture, 2021'). It is not a recurring/periodical publication — it was produced once at the start of Phase 5. The programme has since moved into a new phase, PSNP6, which was approved/launched around March 2026 (World Bank press release, worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2026/03/03/ethiopia-a-new-phase-of-support-for-safety-nets...; World Bank project documents for P511478 'Productive Safety Net Program 6'). Since PSNP5 is already superseded by PSNP6's own separate design/project documents, no further release of 'the PSNP5 Design Document' specifically is expected. Historical PSNP phase lengths have also been irregular (PSNP2 ~2007-2009, PSNP3 2010-2014, PSNP4 2015-2020, PSNP5 2021-2025), so even treating this as a 'per-phase' publication would not yield a fixed/computable cadence.

results.window:
The SEASN project, approved in November 2020, is an Investment Project
    Financing (IPF) with Performance Based Conditions (PBCs). The SEASN project supports the Government of Ethiopia
    (GoE) flagship Productive Safety Net Programme Phase Five (PSNP 5) which provides a predictable safety net for
    Ethiopia’s poorest populations in the form of cash or food transfers to 7.9 million people either in return for
    participation in public works or unconditionally to households without adults who are work-able. PSNP 5 is facing a
    severe financing crisis caused by persistent extreme climate events (droughts) and conflict that have increased
    social protection needs, combined with a reduction in development partner and government financing and
    escalating costs due to the high rates of inflation.

targetReport.title: Consumer Price Index (Ethiopian Statistics Services)
targetReport.description: Ethiopia's official monthly CPI, produced by ESS (formerly the Central Statistical Agency/CSA). VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session via ESS's own site: 'Published monthly', described as 'the principal measure of inflation'; ESS's own framing states its statistics 'support evidence-based policy decisions, wage and income adjustments, business planning, and economic research'. Confirmed via Grok's round: Ethiopia is on the IMF's e-GDDS dissemination tier (not full SDDS), per the IMF's own 2019 press release announcing Ethiopia's e-GDDS implementation -- the same weaker tier already found for Kenya, now a second country on this node. Based on the recent 16-20 day lag, the July 2026 CPI is estimated to post roughly mid-to-late August 2026; this is an estimate, not a published date.

Rate estimated from the latest observed interval (2013→2019, 6 years → ~0.17/yr), per Research.1.md §4's 'latest observed interval' convention for irregular recurring documents; the earlier interval (2001→2013) was 12 years, so this estimate is imprecise and should be revisited if a post-2019 edition surfaces. Retrieved via WebFetch (an AI-summarising intermediary, not a direct page render) — flagged per the AU branch's standing caution against trusting a summarising reader uncritically; the quoted fragments read as exact section headings rather than paraphrase, but a future session should confirm against the raw HTML/PDF if this cadence estimate is ever load-bearing for something more than an isolated node.

release_schedule.note: ISSAI 300 (Performance Audit Principles) is an INTOSAI/IFPP professional pronouncement, not a periodic statistical release. It was endorsed in 2001, substantially reformulated in 2013, and renamed with editorial changes in 2019 under the IFPP. INTOSAI's Due Process for the IFPP states that revision timing is not centrally fixed: 'The working groups decide on an appropriate frequency at which the regular review shall be carried out,' with maintenance frequency to be communicated per-standard on issai.org. As of the current standard-setting projects list on issai.org/standards-in-setting/, ISSAI 300 is not listed as an active revision project, so there is no known upcoming or scheduled next edition. Revisions have occurred irregularly (2001, 2013, 2019) at the discretion of the responsible performance-audit working group rather than on a fixed calendar.

targetReport.title: Supply, Use and Input-Output Tables (SUIOTs)
targetReport.description: Matrices balancing supply and use of products across the economy to compile a single coherent GDP estimate. results.basis: The CRA page opens: 'Each year, certain personal income tax and benefit amounts are indexed to inflation using the Consumer Price Index data as reported by Statistics Canada.' The statutory mechanism is Income Tax Act s. 117.1(1)(b)(ii), which sets the adjustment factor as (A/B) - 1 where 'A is the Consumer Price Index for the 12 month period that ended on September 30 next before that year, and B is the Consumer Price Index for the 12 month period immediately preceding'; s. 117.1(4) defines that index as 'the Consumer Price Index for Canada, as published by Statistics Canada under the authority of the Statistics Act' averaged over the twelve months of the period. The published indexation factors (2.0% for 2026, 2.7% for 2025, 4.7% for 2024, 6.3% for 2023) are the direct output and drive every indexed bracket threshold and credit amount in the CRA table. See also https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/acts/I-3.3/section-117.1.html

results.basis: Canada Pension Plan s. 18(1)(c) sets the Year's Maximum Pensionable Earnings for each year as the preceding year's YMPE multiplied by the ratio of the average Wage Measure for the twelve months ending 30 June of the preceding year to the same average a year earlier. Section 18(5) defines the term: 'The Wage Measure for a month is the average weekly wages and salaries of (a) the Industrial Aggregate in Canada for the month as published by Statistics Canada under the authority of the Statistics Act.' That industrial-aggregate average weekly earnings series is the output of the Survey of Employment, Payrolls and Hours. Section 18(6) further requires that the most recently published Statistics Canada revision of the Industrial Aggregate be used, and s. 18(7) requires the Minister to adjust the series, on the advice of the Chief Statistician, if Statistics Canada changes the time or content basis of the Industrial Aggregate by more than one per cent.

targetReport.publisher: Canada Employment Insurance Commission / Employment and Social Development Canada
targetReport.description: The annual ceiling on earnings on which EI premiums are payable and on which EI benefits are calculated, announced each September for the following year. release_schedule.rule: Employment Insurance Act, s.4: the maximum yearly insurable earnings for a year is 52 times the average, for the 12-month period ending April 30 of the year immediately before that year, of the Average Weekly Earnings of the Industrial Aggregate in Canada (as published by Statistics Canada) for each month in that period, adjusted by the year-over-year percentage change in that average, and rounded down to the nearest multiple of $100.  The number of weeks for which you may receive benefits doesn’t change if you move to another region after your benefit period begins. How we calculate your weekly benefit amount

 The amount of weekly benefits is calculated as follows:

 
 we calculate your total insurable earnings for the required number of best weeks (the weeks that you earned the most money, including insurable tips and commissions) based on the information you provide or your record of employment (ROE)

 we determine the divisor (number of best weeks) that corresponds to your regional rate of unemployment

 we divide your total insurable earnings for your best weeks by your required number of best weeks

 we then multiply the result by 55% to obtain the amount of your weekly benefits

 
 In regions of Canada with the highest rates of unemployment, we’ll calculate using the best 14 weeks. In regions of Canada with the lowest rates of unemployment, we’ll use the best 22 weeks.

targetReport.title: Survey of Household Spending (SHS)
targetReport.description: Annual national household survey collecting detailed information on what Canadian households spend on food, shelter, clothing, transportation and other categories. Its principal downstream use is to supply the expenditure detail used to construct Consumer Price Index basket weights, particularly at low levels of product and geographic aggregation. Results are released as Table 11-10-0222-01 and associated Daily articles.

release_schedule.note: StatCan's own survey metadata (IMDB, SDDS 3508) states the Survey of Household Spending is conducted 'Every 2 years' (reference years 2019, 2021, 2023, 2025, ...), so data collection follows a fixed 2-year cycle. However, there is no published release calendar and the actual publication lag after each reference year has been highly irregular: 2019 reference-year data was released 2021-01-22 (~13 months after year-end), 2021 data was released 2023-10-18 (~22 months after year-end), and 2023 data was released 2025-05-21 (~17 months after year-end) — see The Daily releases dq210122b, dq231018a, and dq250521a. Because both the exact release month and the lag length vary substantially cycle to cycle, no specific next release date can be reliably computed. 2025 reference-year data collection ran through roughly February 2026 per StatCan's respondent portal, so the next release (for 2025 data) is expected at some point in 2026-2027, but no concrete date or calendar entry has been published by StatCan as of 2026-08-11.

results.basis: The organic decentralization law's Article 250 institutes the 'fonds de péréquation des collectivités locales' and Article 252 states it is funded by 'un prélèvement d'office opéré sur le budget général de l'Etat dont le taux est fixé annuellement dans la loi de finances' — i.e. the organic law itself designates the annual Finance Law as the instrument that sets the fund's actual take rate/amount each year. The FY2025 Finance Law's Article 21 line item 712 ('Péréquation Collectivités', 402,261,680 FCFA) is exactly that designated annual act: it is not merely citing the fund for context, it is the yearly mechanism Article 252 names as the fund's funding source, applied. That is a genuine data/figure dependency (the budget line's existence and legal basis flow from Article 252's designation) rather than a loose contextual reference, so uses_data_from is chosen over cites. Not calculated_from, since the 402,261,680 FCFA figure is not itself derived by a stated formula from anything in the organic law — the organic law sets the mechanism (that a rate is fixed annually in the finance law), not the rate itself.

targetReport.title: Loi organique N°001/2014 du 14/06/2015 relative à la décentralisation
targetReport.publisher: Journal Officiel de la République Gabonaise / Présidence de la République
targetReport.description: Gabon's organic decentralization law, published in the Journal Officiel de la République Gabonaise, N°260 du 7 juillet 2015, and signed by President Ali Bongo Ondimba ("Fait à Libreville, le 15 juin 2015"). Defines a commune as "une personne morale de droit public distincte de l'Etat, dotée de la personnalité juridique et de l'autonomie administrative et financière." Classifies communes by population and own-resources: "Article 5 : Les communes de première catégorie sont celles ayant plus de 15 000 habitants ou des ressources propres supérieures ou égales à 150 millions de francs CFA. Article 6 : Les communes de seconde catégorie sont celles dont la population est comprise entre 5000 et 15 000 habitants ou ayant des ressources propres comprises entre 50 et 150 millions de francs CFA." Article 216 requires that competence transfers from the State to communes and départements identify the resulting financial charges, and states the general principle: "Le transfert des compétences s'accompagne du transfert des ressources correspondantes." Establishes State transfers to local government: "Article 238 : Les transferts de l'Etat, sous forme de dotations ou de transferts d'impôts, visent à compenser l'accroissement des charges de la collectivité locale du fait de la décentralisation et de l'insuffisance de ses ressources propres. Article 239 : ... -de la dotation globale de fonctionnement destinée au fonctionnement courant de la collectivité locale ; -des dotations et subventions d'équipement destinées à l'investissement de la collectivité locale ; -de la dotation liée à l'accroissement des charges résultant des transferts des compétences ; -de la dotation visant à compenser le manque à gagner résultant des dégrèvements et exonérations consentis par la loi." Also creates a named equalisation fund: "Article 250 : Il est institué un fonds de péréquation des collectivités locales chargé de fournir aux collectivités locales des ressources additionnelles... Article 252 : Le Fonds de péréquation des collectivités locales est alimenté par : -un prélèvement d'office opéré sur le budget général de l'Etat dont le taux est fixé annuellement dans la loi de finances ; -la contribution respective des collectivités locales dont le taux... tient compte de la capacité contributive de chaque collectivité locale." CAVEAT: a December 2020 secondary news report (Gabonreview, not independently quotable) suggested the Fonds de péréquation's operational status was still "under study" as of that date; no 2021-2026 primary document confirms current operational status, and the implementing décret referenced in Article 253 ("Ses attributions et son organisation sont fixés par les statuts approuvés par décret") could not be located this round.

targetReport.title: Consumer Price Index (Ghana Statistical Service)
targetReport.description: VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session via GSS's own CPI Technical Methodology Manual (v5, published October 2020) and its own recent press releases. The v5 manual: 'GSS uses 13 out of the 15 Divisions as distinguished by the COICOP manual', organised into '44 Groups, 98 Classes, 156 Subclasses, and 307 Item-level observations', and 'to order products into these different categories, GSS uses the United Nations Classification of Individual Consumption According to Purpose (COICOP) 2018 manual.' Elementary aggregates: 'GSS uses the unweighted Jevons Index... the geometric mean of price relatives.' The v5 manual describes the then-current series on 'the whole year of 2018 as the price reference period' with 'weights based on the Ghana Living Standard Surveys 7 (GLSS7) from 2016/2017', and credits input from 'Statistics Denmark, and the International Monetary Fund (IMF)' plus ILO CPI-manual guidance. GSS has since rebased: the September 2025 press release (published 1 October 2025) states 'the price reference period has been updated to 2021 (2021=100)' with the weight reference period still 2017 -- confirmed independently, distinct from and more current than the v5 manual's own 2018=100 description. The rebase's own dedicated methodology note (as opposed to a press-release mention) was not located this session.

targetReport.publisher: República de Guinea Ecuatorial (official constitutional text, hosted by FAOLEX)
targetReport.description: Equatorial Guinea's constitution. Artículo 3, apartados 4-5: "4. Se divide para los fines administrativos y económicos en Regiones, Provincias, Distritos y Municipios. 5. La ley determina los límites y las denominaciones de las regiones, provincias, distritos y municipios." Título Cuarto, "De las Corporaciones Locales," Artículo 131: "Las Corporaciones Locales son instituciones con personalidad jurídica propia, encargadas del gobierno y administración de las regiones, provincias, distritos y municipios. Promueven los planes y programas de desarrollo económico y social de sus respectivos territorios de acuerdo a la ley." Artículo 132.2: "La ley determina las competencias, el funcionamiento, la jurisdicción y la composición de las Corporaciones Locales." The Constitution itself establishes Municipios as one of four administrative/economic-division tiers and gives Corporaciones Locales legal personality, but explicitly delegates all finance/competency detail to ordinary law rather than stating a mechanism itself — the implementing law is Ley Número 1/2003 (see gq-ley-1-2003-administracion-local). Independently downloaded and text-extracted via pdftotext, not AI-summarized. Equatorial Guinea's official BOE portal (boe.gob.gq) could not be reached this round (503 Service Unavailable) to cross-verify against a more-authoritative host; the FAOLEX copy was used and is treated as reliable.

targetReport.title: Harmonized Commodity Description and Coding System (HS)
targetReport.description: The multipurpose international product nomenclature developed by the World Customs Organization: more than 5,000 commodity groups, each identified by a six-digit code. The commodity-side counterpart to the industry classifications already in this corpus — national trade statistics, including Canada's, are coded to it, with countries adding digits beyond six for tariff and statistical detail.
targetReport.cadence_note: The WCO's Harmonized System Committee 'prepares amendments updating the HS every 5 – 6 years' — editions 2002, 2007, 2012, 2017, 2022. Not an annual release; releases_per_year is nominal.

release_schedule.rule: The WCO prepares amendments updating the HS nomenclature every 5-6 years through the Review Sub-Committee and HS Committee; the HS Convention provides a two-and-one-half-year implementation period after adoption before a new edition enters into force (six months for reservations, two years for correlation tables/translation/legislative updates). The HS2022 edition entered into force 1 January 2022; the next edition, originally planned as HS2027, was pushed back one year due to COVID-19-related delays and will be HS2028, entering into force 1 January 2028.
release_schedule.note: This is a periodic amendment/nomenclature update, not a recurring data report with dated calendar entries. The WCO's own site frames it as a 5-6 year revision cycle governed by the HS Convention's implementation timeline rather than a fixed calendar. A further, more fundamental revision (HS2033) is already being planned as a follow-on cycle.

targetReport.title: ICD-10-CA and the Canadian Classification of Health Interventions (CCI)
targetReport.description: The companion Canadian clinical classifications maintained and published by CIHI: ICD-10-CA (the Canadian enhancement of the WHO's ICD-10 for diseases and health problems) and CCI (health interventions). Published together as versioned classification releases with accompanying Canadian Coding Standards, they are the coding standard for hospital data submissions.
targetReport.cadence_note: Versioned releases roughly every three years — v2015, v2018, v2022, with v2025/v2027 enhancement cycles under way — with coding-standard updates in between. releases_per_year is nominal.

release_schedule.rule: CIHI is postponing implementation of new versions of CCI and the Canadian Coding Standards until fiscal year 2027-2028. Separately, CIHI will no longer be updating ICD-10-CA at all, aligning with WHO's 2019 halt of ICD-10 updates as the international community moves toward ICD-11.
release_schedule.note: This report bundles ICD-10-CA and CCI, but the two now have divergent status: ICD-10-CA is permanently frozen (CIHI stated it 'will no longer be updating ICD-10-CA'), so only the CCI component will see a future release. CIHI's most recent bulletin (as of mid-2026) postpones the next CCI/Canadian Coding Standards version to fiscal year 2027-2028 (Apr 1, 2027 - Mar 31, 2028) without a specific date yet announced. Prior versions were labeled 'Version 2018' and 'Version 2022,' and the 2025-2026 Classification Tables (an interim update, not a full new version) were released October 2024.

targetReport.title: Supply, Use and Input-Output Tables
targetReport.description: The annual benchmark of the Canadian System of Macroeconomic Accounts. The supply and use tables trace the production of products by domestic industries, combined with imports, through their use as intermediate inputs or as final consumption, investment or exports, and yield gross value added by industry; the symmetric industry-by-industry input-output tables are derived from them. Record 1401's own description states the tables 'can be used to calculate economy-wide gross domestic product (GDP) either directly, by summing value added over the industries, or indirectly, by summing to the economy-wide cost of primary inputs (income-based GDP) or by computing the grand total of the flow of products into final use categories (expenditure-based GDP) - the link to the national income and expenditure accounts.' Both the monthly GDP by industry programme and the quarterly income and expenditure accounts are projections off this benchmark, which is the actual shape of the Canadian accounts and was not representable in this graph until now.
targetReport.cadence_note: Annual, reference period calendar year, but with an unusually long lag: record 1401 states the tables 'are available about two and half years after the end of the reference year; this is because of the delay in obtaining the needed source data and by the complex nature of producing such a detailed account.' The programme also releases derived products on separate dates — the 2026 release schedule lists April 15 for the input-output tables, May 4 for value added in exports and June 16 for the economic impact of wireless telecommunications carriers — so releases_per_year 1 counts the benchmark tables and not the satellite products.

release_schedule.note: Statistics Canada's IMDB page for SDDS 1401 states supply/use and input-output tables are annual and 'available about two and half years after the end of the reference year' due to data-collection lag. Observed national releases: 2023 reference-year data released 2025-04-14, and 2024 reference-year data released 2026-04-15 (both via The Daily / table pid 3610008401, catalogue 15-207-X). This gives a consistent mid-April annual pattern for the most recent two cycles, implying the 2025 reference-year release would land around April 2027. Earlier years (2017-2022) show more variable timing (June-July, and some Nov/Dec releases), and there is a separate, later-lagged provincial/territorial supply-and-use table release that has landed in November in recent years (e.g. 2025-11-13 for 2022 provincial data) - so the overall SDDS 1401 program has more than one sub-release per year even though releases_per_year=1 on file; treat the April date as the primary/national release this corpus field likely tracks.

targetReport.description: Statistics Canada's official population estimates for Canada, the provinces and the territories, produced by the Demographic Estimates Program (record number 3601) and published as Table 17-10-0009-01. targetReport.title: Canada Health Transfer
targetReport.description: The largest major federal transfer to provinces and territories, providing federal cash support for health care and backing the criteria of the Canada Health Act. The national cash contribution is set in statute at section 24.1 of the Federal-Provincial Fiscal Arrangements Act and escalates each year by a three-year moving average of nominal GDP growth subject to a 3 per cent floor; the national amount is then divided among provinces on an equal per capita basis under section 24.21. Finance Canada publishes provincial and territorial entitlement amounts each year before the start of the fiscal year.
targetReport.cadence_note: The escalator must be determined by the Minister of Finance not later than three months before the beginning of the fiscal year, i.e. by the end of December for the fiscal year starting the following April 1. Entitlements are re-estimated several times during and after the year under the CHT/CST Regulations, but there is one authoritative annual determination.

Confirmed instances: Dec 2021 (for 2022-23), Dec 2022 (for 2023-24), Dec 15 2023 (for 2024-25), Dec 23 2024 (for 2025-26), and the major-federal-transfers.html table was updated Dec 11 2025 showing 2026-27 amounts (consistent with a Dec 2025 announcement). targetReport.title: Alberta Health Services Business Plan and Health Plan
targetReport.description: The annual business plan and accompanying budget that Alberta Health Services is required to prepare and submit to the Minister under sections 9(1) and 9.1(1) of the Provincial Health Agencies Act, with the business plan itself required under section 10 of the Sustainable Fiscal Planning and Reporting Act. It states the funding AHS expects to receive from Alberta Health and from Mental Health and Addiction for the coming year and sets the service and performance commitments those funds buy. It is the document that converts a provincial budget number into an operating plan for the province's largest health delivery organization.
targetReport.cadence_note: Board-approved in late March, immediately after the provincial budget is tabled in February, then submitted to the Minister for approval.

release_schedule.note: AHS's own Health Plan & Business Plan landing page (https://www.albertahealthservices.ca/about/page13365.aspx) still lists the 2024-27 Health Plan and 2024-25 Business Plan (both 'Prepared September 2024') as current as of August 2026 -- no 2025-26 or later edition exists (a direct guess at the expected filename ahs-org-bp-2025-2026.pdf returns 404). Historically the cadence was already uneven (2019-23, 2020-23, then 2023-2024 prepared April 2023, then 2024-2025 prepared September 2024 -- gaps of multiple years, inconsistent month). More importantly, AHS's Board of Directors was dissolved in January 2025 as part of a government-mandated split of AHS into four new agencies (Acute Care Alberta / renamed 'Hospital and Surgical Health Services', Primary Care Alberta, Recovery Alberta, Assisted Living Alberta), a restructuring substantially completed by late 2025. AHS continues to exist as a service-delivery body under the oversight of these new agencies, but there is no evidence it has published (or committed to publish) a new standalone AHS Business Plan/Health Plan since Sept 2024, and Government of Alberta ministry-level business plans (e.g., 'Hospital and Surgical Health Services Business Plan 2026-29') now appear to be the vehicle for forward-looking planning documents in this space. No calendar, no stated rule, and the prior loose pattern has been broken by the reorg -- this is genuinely irregular/unscheduled going forward.

targetReport.title: Treaty for the Establishment of a BRICS Contingent Reserve Arrangement (Fortaleza, 15 July 2014)
targetReport.publisher: Governments of the Federative Republic of Brazil, the Russian Federation, the Republic of India, the People's Republic of China and the Republic of South Africa
targetReport.description: International treaty establishing a self-managed Contingent Reserve Arrangement (CRA) of USD 100 billion among the five founding BRICS members. Signed in Fortaleza on 15 July 2014. Purpose: provide liquidity and precautionary instruments in response to actual or potential short-term balance-of-payments pressures; complement the global financial safety net (IMF, bilateral swaps, own reserves). Individual commitments: China USD 41 bn; Brazil, India, Russia USD 18 bn each; South Africa USD 5 bn. Entered into force after all parties completed domestic procedures (announced at 7th BRICS Summit 2015). Resources remain with national central banks until drawn via currency swap.

targetReport.title: Consumer Price Index Manual: Concepts and Methods
targetReport.publisher: IMF, ILO, OECD, Eurostat, UNECE and the World Bank
targetReport.description: The internationally agreed manual of concepts, methods and practice for compiling a consumer price index. Jointly published by six international organisations and managed by the IMF; the 2020 edition updates the 2004 ILO-managed Consumer Price Index Manual: Theory and Practice. Country code is CA only because the schema offers no international option — the publisher is a consortium of international agencies.
targetReport.cadence_note: Revised roughly once a generation — editions in 1989, 2004 and 2020. Not an annual release; releases_per_year is nominal so the pulse rate reads as near-static.

release_schedule.note: No release calendar or stated periodicity exists. The Manual has been issued only three times: 1989 (ILO, 'Consumer Price Indices: An ILO Manual'), 2004 ('Consumer Price Index Manual: Theory and Practice'), and 2020 ('Consumer Price Index Manual: Concepts and Methods'), each ~15-16 years apart. The IMF's own page for this report is titled 'Update of the Consumer Price Index Manual' and explains the 2020 edition was produced because 'methods and best practices have continued to evolve' since 2004, following requests from the 2014 UNECE-ILO CPI Experts Meeting -- i.e., updates are triggered by inter-agency expert consensus, not a fixed schedule. No next-edition date or working-group timeline is published. This is consistent with the corpus's very low releases_per_year (0.06, i.e. roughly once per 16 years).

targetReport.title: EAC Regulations for Compiling Harmonised Consumer Price Indices (HCPI)
targetReport.description: A binding East African Community instrument (March 2022) requiring Partner States to compile and submit a Harmonised CPI to the EAC Secretariat, for regional comparability and East African Monetary Union convergence-criteria monitoring -- described as binding in its entirety and directly applicable, and classification 'shall be based on the most recent official United Nations Classification of Individual Consumption According to Purpose (COICOP)'.
